subject: Intermittent large-packet egress stalls after private cutover
messages:
From: Emily Zhang <emily@highpine.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Highpine Network Ops <ops@highpine.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment cutover — intermittent egress stalls

Marissa,

We finished the VPC cutover to the new private connectivity yesterday evening. Since then we've seen intermittent stalls when moving large files out of our on-prem warehouse to S3 (uploads hang for ~30-90s and then resume). Small transfers are fine. The pattern looks like large-packet bursts (we're using 9000 byte MTU across the crossconnect).

Attached: a short pcap (capture_p50.pcap) showing three upload attempts, and a traceroute I ran during an incident (netdiag_traceroutes.txt).

Quick facts:
- Affected path: On-prem -> Crossconnect -> Redwood Private front-door -> upstream cloud region (us-west-2)
- Symptoms: TCP stalls, retransmit bursts, then resume; throughput drops sharply during stall
- Time window: began ~2026-11-17 20:30 UTC after cutover finished

Can you confirm whether Redwood applies any MTU clipping, MSS clamping, or SNAT that might break large frames? Happy to run any captures or provide logs. This is impacting nightly ETL jobs.

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Zhang
Director, Infrastructure
Highpine Analytics

Emily — thanks for the clear summary and the pcap. Sorry you're hitting this right after cutover.

Initial thoughts:
- Our platform can do MSS clamping on the TCP path and we also have automatic PMTU discovery, but if there are devices in the middle doing fragmentation or dropping large-fragmented packets, that could cause retransmits/stalls.
- SNAT shouldn't affect MTU directly, but conntrack translation + a middlebox rewriting may trigger packet drops when jumbo frames are used.

Immediate triage steps I've asked Markus and Neha to run:
1) Check for any recent egress NAT/SNAT rules changes on your Dedicated pool and whether we introduced a path that toggles between SNAT and passthrough during cutover.
2) Inspect the front-door (private egress proxy) for fragmentation/DF-bit behavior and any kernel logs about ICMP 'frag needed'.
3) Correlate our front-door connection logs to your timestamps for dropped retransmissions.

Next actions for you (if convenient):
- If you can, rerun the upload while capturing TCP dumps on your on-prem egress and share a 60s window.
- Also share if your routers are intentionally set to 9000 MTU end-to-end (some switches rewrite DF).

I'll escalate if we find device-level reassembly failures. Looping in Markus & Neha to take this on.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Manager, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference

Hi team — I pulled the attached pcap and the front-door kernel logs during the timestamps Emily sent. Quick notes from initial analysis:
- I see a consistent pattern where uploads start, then a burst of retransmits occurs when MSS-sized segments exceed path MTU and the DF bit is set. We're getting ICMP "Fragmentation needed" in some cases, but it's not always delivered back to origin due to an intermediate firewall that suppresses ICMP in some flows.
- There's also a conntrack entry for those flows showing SNAT applied on the front-door node; TTLs and port translation are normal.
- The crossconnect preserves 9000 MTU on our side, but one of the customer's upstream on-prem switches is clipping to 1500 in practice (it looks like GSO/GRO interaction issue combined with offload).

Recommendation:
1) Temporarily enable MSS clamping at the front-door egress (set MSS to 1400) for the affected prefix to prevent DF-bit stalls. This is low-risk and should immediately stop the stalls.
2) In parallel, customer-side: verify NIC offload settings (GSO/GRO) and set MTU consistently end-to-end, or disable offload during the window.
3) If MSS clamping helps, we'll keep it in a targeted rule and plan for a coordinated MTU alignment with Highpine.

Emily — can you run a quick test with a new capture after I toggle MSS clamping? I'll schedule the change for 13:00 PT and post back.

-Markus
Network Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
